Deuteronomy 6:25 calls observing the commandments “our righteousness”; Psalm 119:172 identifies the commandments themselves as righteousness; and 1 John 3:7 explicitly argues that the person doing righteousness is righteous. Revelation 19:8 further identifies the wedding linen as the saints’ righteous acts. The strongest counter-reading rightly treats righteousness as a broader, context-sensitive category encompassing conformity to God’s will, right status, divine justice, and ethical conduct. But for the evidence actually used to establish the entry, that counter-reading includes rather than displaces the book’s referent. It therefore does not furnish a materially contradictory explanation.
